newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes quiet on Friday, seen toppy.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes quiet on Friday, seen toppy.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed virtually unchanged on Friday after trading in a narrow range against the U.S. currency.
At the close the TWI was off five basis points at 67.39.
Against the greenback the kiwi traded between 0.7068 and 0.7081, closing at 0.7070.
"It has been absolutely dead actually," a Wellington-based chief dealer said.

"The range has been 0.7068-81 and it is pretty quiet. I think it is starting to struggle up here. I would like to see it a little lower myself. I think maybe it is time to have another test down at (the support level of) 0.7020," he said.

Dealers said the political situation had gone quiet since the announcement of the coalition deal between the conservatuive National Party and nationalist New Zealand First, although there was an expectation of further initiatives in the New Year.

The chief dealer said news that NZ First leader and Treasurer Winston Peters would take responsibility for the Reserve Bank and the foreign investment watchdog the Overseas Investment Commission was expected.
"I think now it is a case of getting throught the Christmas New Year period when there are generally more sellers than buyers.
"Generally you see a lot of positions squared up at this time of year," he said.
He said offshore investors have been long in the kiwi and he expected those positions to be settled in the next few days.
